person.name: Johannes Makkinga
person.relationshipContext: father of Gerrit Makkinga (1922); direct ancestor

researchFocus: railway career, residences and household movements in the 1920s-1930s

runSelection.question: Kan Johannes Makkinga's werk bij de Nederlandse Spoorwegen en zijn verhuizing naar Pijnacker in 1934 betrouwbaar worden gereconstrueerd?
runSelection.value: A railway occupation plus successive residences can turn a bare ancestor record into a chronological working-life biography.

claims.claim: A local-history reconstruction of Pijnacker's Stationsstraat identifies Johannes Makkinga, born 2 October 1895 in Stad Ommen, and Everijntje Schoonderbeek, born 19 May 1895 in Veenendaal, as residents there in 1934.

source.title: Pijnacker in vroeger tijden - Stationsstraat
source.sourceType: local-history reconstruction; underlying register not yet inspected

claims.claim: The same reconstruction describes Johannes as 'assistent bij de N.S.'
claims.reason: Specific and identity-compatible secondary/local-history statement, but the underlying railway personnel or population record has not yet been inspected.

claims.claim: Johannes came to Pijnacker around mid-July 1934 from Borculo, while Everijntje came from Wolvega.
claims.reason: Reported by the same local-history reconstruction; requires confirmation in population registers/family cards.

claims.claim: Children named in the Pijnacker reconstruction are Gerrit (2 March 1922 Enschede), Aaltje (7 January 1924 Enschede), Henri (2 May 1927 Sint Annaparochie), and Hendrikus (7 September 1934 Pijnacker).
claims.reason: Useful household chronology but each child/date should be checked against civil/population records before publication as confirmed biography.
